name: OpenClip
one_liner: Select text in any Mac app; a floating bar offers copy, transform, math and AI actions

text.why: OpenClip reads the selected text through macOS Accessibility (not the clipboard) on macOS 14+ and shows a bar of actions that fit it. Pressing ⌥⌘C turns the bar into a fuzzy-search palette over the whole action catalog, and extensions are JavaScript, AppleScript, shell or URL-template files dropped into ~/.openclip/extensions with an openclip.json manifest, no compile step. AI actions can run on Apple Intelligence, a local Ollama model, or OpenAI/Claude.
text.take: It is plainly an open-source PopClip alternative with a simpler extension format; the trade-off is an app that cannot work without Accessibility permission.
build: One openclip.json with a URL template becomes a search action for your internal wiki or order lookup; a shell-script extension can send a selected product code to an inventory API and surface the result as a status message or notification.

who.role: Mac users who handle a lot of text
who.situation: case changes, summaries, translations on selection
register shell or JS scripts as text-selection actions
inline AI writing on a local model, no cloud

start.text: # launch OpenClip and grant Accessibility permission:
System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility → enable OpenClip
# select text in any app, or press ⌥⌘C

caveat: MIT. macOS 14+ only and Accessibility permission is mandatory.
Cloud AI (OpenAI, Claude) uses your own API key and budget; choosing Apple Intelligence or a local Ollama model needs no cloud key.
The README states it is independent of and unaffiliated with PopClip.
